NEW - BLOCKING
N1 - REQ-001 AC4, rule (б) (R2). The marks depend on when the journal is read, and one hand-written line eventually hides real work. Rule (б) judges a line against «часов компьютера в момент чтения», so a line dated in the future stops being marked once the clock comes within 60 s of its time. Rule (в) then uses it as the latest time and marks every later real line that is more than 120 s earlier.
Example:
  - The journal has a real line at 10:00, a hand-written REAL line dated 11:00 (appended at 10:00:30), then real lines at 10:01, 10:30 and 10:59.
  - Read at 10:05: only the 11:00 line is marked.
  - Read at or after 10:59:00: the 11:00 line counts, and the real lines at 10:01 and 10:30 are marked «не из хуков» and drop out of the tasks.
The same journal gives different marks at different times, and a forged line ends up hiding almost an hour of real work. The AC4 test uses a fixed clock and cannot see this.
Fix:
  - Every line's mark except the last line's depends only on the journal content. Judge a forward-dated line by the lines after it. One way: a line is «не из хуков» when the next line is more than 120 s earlier than it but fits the lines before it; use the clock rule only for a line with nothing after it.
  - State that the server appends lines in the order it accepts them; the 120 s argument relies on that.
  - Tests: the same journal read at now and at now+2 h gives identical marks. A line dated +1 h followed by an hour of real lines marks only that line, at both read times. A back-dated line after real lines marks only itself.

N2 - REQ-001 AC6(в) and «Сбои»; REQ-007 AC1 and its description («идущая сессия») (R2). Both treat a session_id as ended forever once any session-end event arrives. cli-reference, --fork-session: «When resuming, create a new session ID instead of reusing the original». So --resume, --continue and interactive /resume keep the same session_id. The hooks page also lists SessionStart source «resume» and SessionEnd reason «resume». In a resumed session, which is the owner's normal path when he reopens a conversation, a subagent running now would show «окончание не записано», and the session would not count as running. The rule as written («в сессии, для которой пришло событие окончания сессии»; «нет события окончания сессии») does not say the order matters, and neither test includes a resume.
Fix:
  - A session-end event counts only for tasks started before it.
  - A session is running if it has an event after the last server start and its last event is not a session-end.
  - Test in both: session-end, then SessionStart (resume) with the same session_id, then a subagent start. The task must be «в работе» and the session must count as running.

NEW - MINOR (fix in the same rework)
N3 - REQ-001 AC14 (Q6; same class as m2, AP-014). ESLint also takes numeric severities, and `grep -nwE 'off|warn|ignores'` does not see them. In a scratch copy, adding `"no-undef": 0` made eslint pass on browser code (`document`; exit 0), while that grep still exited 1. Without the line, eslint exits 1. Fix: allow eslint.config.js to gain only a files + languageOptions.globals block. Check for example `grep -c rules tools/eslint.config.js` = 1 (today's block only), or add a grep for numeric severities that must exit 1.

N4 - REQ-007 AC6. The criterion says «нет встроенных скриптов и обработчиков в атрибутах», but `grep -rnE ' on[a-z]+='` misses `onClick=`: HTML attribute names ignore case, so it works in a browser. It also misses inline `<script>` blocks. Dry runs: onclick 0, onClick 1, an inline script block 1. Fix: grep -i, and a check that every `<script>` in the served HTML has src. The latter can go in the office test or pixel-office-server.test.js.

N5 - REQ-001 AC3 and AC4. The SessionStart hook input has its own field named source (startup, resume, clear, compact, fork; hooks «SessionStart input»). The journal's allowed key is also called source (REAL or SIMULATION), and AC4 answers 400 to any body with source. A hook that forwards input.source would lose every SessionStart silently, since AC10 keeps it quiet. The AC3 test would still pass: it checks only that written lines have allowed keys, and a line that was never written passes that vacuously. Fix: AC3 says the SessionStart input field source is not the journal's source and is never sent. The AC3 test also requires that each connected event's example produces exactly one journal line.

Notes, no change required:
- AC1(в)/(ж) cannot observe SessionEnd handlers. Per the SDK, includeHookEvents emits a hook_response for SessionEnd only for background hooks. AC10's test covers them.
- The description line «в объявлении прогона его пока нет» (STATE.md) is true. It could say instead that REQ-006 AC14 allows STATE.md for every run.
